children: Gold prices fall further, with New York futures now below the $4,400-a-troy-ounce mark after wholesale-price inflation in the U.S. sped up in August. "The key components of the PPI that feed into the core PCE deflator were fairly strong in August, raising the chance of the Fed hiking interest rates next week," says Stephen Brown, chief economist for North America at Capital Economics. Traders are now pricing in a roughly 70% chance of a rate hike by the Federal Reserve next week, up from 60% earlier Thursday, according to the FedWatch tool. In early U.S. trading, gold is down 1.5% to $4,392.90 an ounce, pressured by a stronger dollar and rising bond yields. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
